reaction.episode: DIGESTION episode, settled data through Oct 16 (dataStale is false; Sunday afternoon run, so Friday's close is the latest settled tape): SPX closed 7,659.44, -2.36% from its 120-day high, 0.61% below its 50-day (7,706.42) but 5.34% above its 200-day (7,271.44). SMH closed $539.79 — just below the Zone 1 floor of $540 after a -10.53% 5-day run, BETWEEN_ZONES — while NVDA at $214.13 remains ABOVE_ZONE_1 ($200-210); VIX spiked to 19.99 (+21.45%) with no rollover, HY OAS is calm at 3.23%, and the mechanical capitulation tally is only 1 of 4 (credit calm alone).
reaction.invalidation: The Watch stance assumes a credit-calm digestion above the 200-day. It is wrong if HY OAS cracks through 4.00% or SPX loses 7,271.44 — that is a regime break, not a buy zone — and equally wrong on the other side if SPX closes above 7,820 with VIX under 17, which would mean the episode ended without ever offering a zone entry.

ladder.response: Move from Watch to Probe: first tranche per the standing zone plan, sized as a probe, not a full position.
ladder.trigger: Escalation down: SMH closes inside Zone 2 ($470-505) or NVDA closes inside Zone 2 ($175-185), with the mechanical tally at 3 of 4 or better and HY OAS still under 4.00%

ladder.response: Re-arm the Zone 1 case and reassess stance to Probe at the next refresh; a single intraday poke above $540 does not count.
ladder.trigger: Zone 1 restored: SMH reclaims and holds a close at or above $565 (top of Zone 1) on a volume-climax reversal (close in the upper part of the range), tally at 2 of 4 or better

ladder.response: No chasing and no adds into the failure zone. Treat it as the pivot-and-fail test: only a held close above SMH $600 / SPX 7,820 converts it; rejection there keeps Watch and re-arms the Zone 2 wait.
ladder.trigger: Trap case: a bounce carries SMH into the $580-600 failure zone or SPX into 7,750-7,820 while the 10-year is still at or above 5.10%

ladder.response: Stand down entirely — the digestion thesis is void, no bottom-fishing at any zone, reassess defensively at the next refresh.
ladder.trigger: Regime break: SPX closes below its 200-day (7,271.44), SMH closes below $470, or HY OAS widens through 4.00%

ladder.response: Episode closed as digestion, not capitulation: return to Hold posture on the core and evaluate DATA_AHEAD names (AVGO, VRT) on their normal promotion gates rather than episode rules.
ladder.trigger: Re-entry / episode over: SPX closes back above its 50-day (7,706.42) with VIX closing under 17

reaction.trapRisk: The expected path is a sudden pivot up that fails — VIX has spiked but not rolled over (5-day high equals the close at 19.99) and the tally is 1 of 4, so the first bounce is the trap, not the bottom. Entries therefore wait for the failure-zone verdict (SMH $580-600 / SPX 7,750-7,820): no buying the first green days, no leveraged vehicles held through the chop, and any probe waits for either Zone 2 occupancy with tally confirmation or a held close above the failure zone.

strategyPosture: Hold the core and stay in Watch on new risk: fundamentals in the AI complex are ahead of price (AVGO +55% revenue at -33.6% from high), but the episode's entry mechanics are not met (tally 1 of 4, SMH below its Zone 1 floor), credit is calm (HY OAS 3.23%), and the Oct 27-28 FOMC sits directly ahead — cash in bills is a position, not a failure.

themes.counterRead: Narrative and data agree on rotation for now, but the agreement rests on one leg: loose credit. The divergence itself is real, and if lending standards tighten or HY OAS widens, the same Mag7 weakness stops being rotation and becomes the leading edge of a rollover — the read flips without the index level changing much.
themes.dataAnchor: The calm is a weighting illusion: the Mag7 average sits 12.19% below its highs versus SPY at -2.4%, a 9.79-point divergence gap, with TSLA the weakest at -28.9% and AAPL strongest at -1.3%. What keeps this a rotation rather than a rollover is credit: SLOOS bank lending standards are LOOSE at 0%, far below the ~40% stress threshold, and HY OAS is contained at 3.23%. Small caps are not confirming calm, though — IWM is -5.45% over 1 month and -8.7% over 3 months.
themes.label: Leadership rotation, not a broad rollover
themes.narrative: The index looks calm — SPY is only 2.4% below its 52-week high — so the tape reads as a shallow, orderly pullback.
themes.watchFor: HY OAS widening above 4.00% or SLOOS tightening off 0% converts rotation into rollover; a Mag7/SPY divergence gap narrowing back under 5 points confirms rotation resolving.

themes.counterRead: This is a multiple-and-positioning washout, not a demand break — yet. The divergence is the opportunity, but it is not yet an entry: the mechanical capitulation tally is only 1 of 4 and SMH closed below its Zone 1 floor, so the data-ahead setup still needs the episode's entry conditions, not just cheapness.
themes.dataAnchor: Revenue says the opposite. AVGO is growing revenue 55% YoY with a 67.8% gross margin and $26.9B FCF while trading 33.6% below its high at RSI 34.8 — the book's top conviction score (82, Tier A). NVDA revenue is growing 61.4% YoY at only -12% from its high. VRT revenue is growing 27.7% YoY while the stock is 45.7% below its high at RSI 27.3. MU is 30% below its high at RSI 34 with the decline classified sentiment-driven. Every one of these dislocations is tagged SENTIMENT_DRIVEN, not fundamental.
themes.label: AI infrastructure: fundamentals ahead of price
themes.narrative: The AI build-out is being repriced as if demand is rolling over: the complex sold off hard into Friday (QQQ -2.77% on the day, SMH -10.53% over 5 days).
themes.watchFor: A hyperscaler capex trim would void the DATA_AHEAD read; SMH reclaiming and holding $540 with a volume-climax reversal restores the Zone 1 entry case.

themes.counterRead: Price ran ahead of fundamentals and is now mean-reverting violently — this is the cautionary tail of the same AI-power story the book owns through VST. The divergence to respect: contracted, cash-generating power (VST +5.18% 1m, RSI 52.4) is holding while pre-revenue names collapse; treating them as one theme misprices both.
themes.dataAnchor: The unwind is the worst in the tracked universe: SMR -36.08% and ASTS -35.18% over one month, OKLO -29.72%, RKLB -24.87% — and Friday accelerated it (ASTS -8.57%, RKLB -7.78%, OKLO -7.15% on the day). These names lead the laggard board while quality AI infrastructure fell far less. The book holds no SMR/OKLO/ASTS/RKLB; its nuclear exposure is VST, which is +5.18% over 1 month with $1.17M of insider buying at the trough.
themes.label: Speculative nuclear/space complex in full unwind
themes.narrative: Small nuclear and space names were priced as if commercial timelines were near and funding was free at a 5.10% 10-year.
themes.watchFor: SMR/OKLO stabilizing above their Friday lows for 5+ sessions would mark unwind exhaustion; further -10% weeks say the speculative purge is still the dominant flow.

themes.counterRead: Narrative (inflation panic) and data (real-rate/term pressure with anchored breakevens) point to different trades. If this were an inflation break, breakevens would lead; they are not. The ceiling breaks the most rate-sensitive equity first — small caps and long-duration speculation — while cash-generative large caps digest. The FOMC is the dated test of which read is right.
themes.dataAnchor: The composition matters: the 10-year is 5.10% but breakeven inflation (T10YIE) is contained at 2.35% — the pressure is a 2.75% real 10-year, not unanchored inflation expectations. The curve is +33bp (2Y 4.77%, 30Y 5.44%), fed funds 3.88%, and credit is not validating panic: HY OAS 3.23% and calm. The damage is concentrated where a real-rate ceiling bites hardest: IWM -8.7% over 3 months versus SPY -0.18% over 1 month.
themes.label: A real-rate ceiling, not an inflation panic
themes.narrative: Rate-hike jitters into the Oct 27-28 FOMC are the stated reason for the selloff — Nasdaq down on AI woes and rate fears, with the Sep CPI event still active.
themes.watchFor: T10YIE pushing above 2.60% would convert this into a genuine inflation problem; a weekly 10-year close back under 5.00% relieves the ceiling.

watchFor: Mechanical capitulation tally reaching at least 3 of 4 (zone occupancy plus VIX rollover plus a volume-climax reversal, with credit calm) — currently 1 of 4
SMH close below $470 (Zone 2 floor) or SPX close below its 200-day at 7,271.44 = regime break, stand down
HY OAS widening through 4.00% from 3.23% = credit crack, voids the rotation read
VIX closing back under 17 after spiking to 19.99 = spike-and-rollover leg of capitulation confirmed
Oct 27-28 FOMC: a hawkish hold with the 10-year pushing above 5.25% extends the ceiling; a weekly 10-year close under 5.00% relieves it
whereWaveBuilds: The next move builds in the AI complex between here and Zone 2 (SMH $470-505 / NVDA $175-185): either capitulation completes there with the tally confirming, or the first bounce runs into the SMH $580-600 / SPX 7,750-7,820 failure zone and the pivot-and-fail verdict decides the quarter's positioning.
